text.p: The Falkland Islands government on Monday said it would issue licenses to 13 companies to explore for oil in waters to the north of the British territory.
Chief Executive of the Falklands Islands government Andrew Gurr said a joint application from British Gas and Argentina's Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales (YPF) was the only bid that failed.
"That was the only consortium that got nothing but that was partly because they limited their bidding to the two most successful tranches," Gurr told Reuters.
But Gurr said the next licensing round would "almost certainly" cover an area of special cooperation which straddles the median line between the Islands and the Argentinian mainland.
Seven tranches were awarded, equal to about 48 North Sea blocks, and covering an area of roughly 12,800 square kilometres.

The seven consortium are as follows: Tranche A will be operated by Amerada Hess with Fina Exploration, Murphy South Atlantic, Teikoku Oil and Argos Evergreen Ltd and Tranche B by Shell Exploration with Agip as partner.
Tranche C&D will be operated by LASMO and include Clyde Expro and newly formed Falklands oil company desire Petroleum.
Tranche F will operated by International Petroleum Corporation with Sands Petroleum.
Tranches I&L were awarded to Desire Petroleum.
